You're on Voat, so I'll assume you won't need much academic advice. As for socializing in high school, do that thing everyone has probably been telling you to do for some time now: be yourself.

I was a band geek in high school. The kind of band geek no one thinks is cool, no one thinks is fun, and that no one would want to sleep with. At the time, this depressed me. I tried to fit in, tried to date girls I didn't really like (or just crushed hard on girls I figured were "too good for me"), and eventually quit the one thing I really enjoyed (band) because it wasn't cool. It wasn't until I got to college and realized that playing instruments was cool. Being in a band was cool. Acting in a play is cool. Dancing is cool. ANYTHING can be cool. Even D&D (who am I kidding? Especially D&D). People are not cool because of the things they do -- people are cool because they are passionate about the things they do. Because they enjoy the things they do. Because the things they do are the things they love, and damn what anybody else thinks of their hobbies. Cool people don't play to the crowd; rather, they attract a crowd of like-minded people who feel comfortable around them.

TL;DR: I wish I knew to be positive, be open, be passionate, and be myself.

All our cats were declawed at the vet, under general anaesthetic and they stay under vet's care for 2-3 days afterwards and are given pain patches until they completely heal.
